Noncalls are coverage/control-dependent and do not certify globally unmethylated adenosines.

name: ac4C mapping and mRNA stability/translation (Arango et al., 2018)
description: Study combining endogenous ac4C-enrichment maps with RNA abundance, ribosome profiling and stability endpoints plus targeted reporter validation.

observation_unit: An enriched ac4C interval or transcript-specific expression/translation/stability measurement under a condition.

labels.name: ac4C-enriched region
labels.meaning: Antibody-enriched interval, not a resolved acetylated nucleotide.

labels.name: translation efficiency
labels.meaning: Ribosome-density relative to mRNA abundance, as defined in the source.

labels.name: mRNA half-life
labels.meaning: Assay-fitted transcript stability endpoint; units/schema require table inspection.

scale.basis: Counted live GEO Series_sample_id fields; cannot be used as a per-assay count.

evidence.supports: Live GEO metadata confirms RIP, RNA-seq, Ribo-seq and BRIC-seq components.
Original article distinguishes ac4C enrichment, transcript half-life, ribosome-density efficiency and targeted reporters.

limitations: No biological data file was inspected; this record establishes resource metadata and documented endpoints only.

cell_specificity.notes: Source context annotations do not by themselves establish cell-selective function.

NAT10 perturbation can affect multiple RNA processes; association alone is not a pure cis ac4C effect.
Targeted synthetic reporters are not a large chemistry-specific reporter-library dataset.
Keep mRNA abundance, half-life and translation efficiency as different labels.

name: Sample et al. 2019 chemistry-specific 5′ UTR reporter libraries
description: Synthetic reporter-library measurements with separately labeled U, pseudouridine and N1-methylpseudouridine RNA chemistries.
biological_context: Pooled reporter mRNAs assayed in HEK293T cells; chemistry-specific eGFP replicate pairs, mCherry and other library subsets must remain distinct.
observation_unit: A reporter-library member × RNA chemistry × experiment, with fraction counts and derived mean ribosome load.

labels.name: RNA chemistry
labels.meaning: Experimental U/Ψ/m1Ψ chemistry class, not an endogenous site annotation.

labels.name: mean ribosome load (MRL)
labels.meaning: Fraction-weighted estimate of reporter ribosome occupancy.

labels.name: polysome distribution
labels.meaning: Relative reporter counts across polysome fractions.

scale.basis: Counted live series/sample metadata; six samples are paired chemistry-specific eGFP libraries, not six independent variant sets.

Live sample metadata confirms paired eGFP unmodified/pseudo/m1pseudo CSV files.
Original paper defines MRL, HEK293T context and chemistry-specific reporter measurements.
Author README links processed CSVs to GEO; repository code license is separate from data reuse rights.

limitations: No biological data file was inspected; this record establishes resource metadata and documented endpoints only.
No processed table header or biological data row was downloaded.
GEO describes a 300,000-member randomized library whereas the paper analyzes 280,000; no unified construct count is asserted.

MRL is an assay-derived translation proxy, not direct protein concentration, half-life or degradation rate.
Treat chemistry and reporter context as explicit variables; shared library members/replicates require leakage-aware grouping.
A canonical-U control is experimentally defined for this library, unlike unobserved sites in endogenous maps.

Raw signal archive and benchmark split membership were not inspected.
The same paper reuses other DRS/orthogonal datasets; they are not counted as newly generated observations here.

integration_caveats: Synthetic chemistry labels and orthogonal-assay labels have different evidential strength.

Modification calibration data do not measure therapeutic-mRNA expression or degradation.

name: NanoBaseLib

observation_unit: A raw/read-level signal, aligned event, or site label depending on benchmark task.

DNA, poly(A) and basecalling observations are not RNA modification labels.
Absent source modification calls are not automatically true negatives; retain each subset's control definition.
Benchmark performance from a fixed preprocessing/basecaller release does not transfer automatically to new chemistry.

Correction content and full supplementary benchmark definitions require review before numerical reuse.

This is primarily rRNA evidence; it is not a mammalian synthetic mRNA expression dataset.
Repeated mixtures/subsampling of the same molecules are not independent biological examples.
